question.problem:
In the figure below, $m\angle{CAD}=100^\circ.$ What is the measure of $\angle{D}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191212/assets/59bb54f508b8045eeffb7cdbf547b6be0f074009b3288fb13e115159909782a8.png)
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $\triangle{ABC}$ is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to $60^\circ\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
m\angle{BAC}=m\angle{ABC}=m\angle{C}=60^\circ
$$

Also, since $\triangle{ADB}$ is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m\angle{BAD}=m\angle{ABD}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191212/assets/a997837f549d59b2a554bf6bc60d9de3ebf6b4b97188ac3d0f07342fb4af6507.png)

Now, since we're told that $m\angle{CAD}=100^\circ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BAD & =m∠CAD-m∠BAC \\  & ={100}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={40}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in $\triangle{BAD}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BAD+m∠D+m∠ABD & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠BAD+m∠D & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2\cdot {40}^{∘}+m∠D & ={180}^{∘} \\ {80}^{∘}+m∠D & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠D & ={100}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
